articles.title: Ventola Projects Installs Immersive Bowling Experience at Ecuador FEC
articles.summary: Ventola Projects completed its first South American project at PlayGo Entertainment in Mall del Alto, Cuenca, Ecuador, delivering ball-responsive projection technology across a bowling venue. The UK firm partnered with US-based VAvR Alliance partner Evogence to bring the immersive system to market. This signals growing international demand for upgraded bowling experiences that blend traditional lanes with cutting-edge projection tech.

articles.title: Indoor Entertainment Drives UAE Attractions Boom
articles.summary: Indoor entertainment is cited as a primary engine behind a significant surge in attractions development across the UAE. The trend reflects broader global appetite for climate-controlled, year-round FEC-style venues in hot-weather markets. FEC operators and investors looking for expansion opportunities should take note of the Middle East as a high-growth region.

articles.title: Slick City and Activeon Accelerate European Expansion with New Parks in Sweden and Austria
articles.summary: Indoor slide park concept Slick City is partnering with Activeon to open new locations in Sweden and Austria, marking a significant push into the European FEC market. The expansion highlights the growing international viability of active-entertainment concepts beyond their North American origins. European FEC operators should watch this trend as competition for leisure spending intensifies.

articles.title: Fun Spot America to Auction Atlanta Park Equipment Following Permanent Closure
articles.summary: Fun Spot America Theme Parks announced that equipment and assets from its permanently closed Atlanta location will go to auction on October 14, 2026. The park shut its doors to guests on August 2, 2026, representing a notable contraction for the regional FEC chain. Operators and suppliers looking for competitively priced used amusement equipment should mark the auction date.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, drawing an outpouring of community sentiment. The closure underscores ongoing challenges facing mid-sized FEC operators navigating post-pandemic competitive and cost pressures. Industry stakeholders should examine the factors behind this closure as a cautionary case study.

articles.title: Japanese Arcade and Entertainment Brand Selects Haywood Mall for First South Carolina Location
articles.summary: A Japanese arcade and entertainment center chain has chosen Haywood Mall in South Carolina for its first location in the state, continuing the trend of Asian FEC concepts expanding aggressively into U.S. mall spaces. The move illustrates how mall-based FEC operators face increasing competition from internationally established brands with strong gaming and entertainment formats. Local operators should prepare for elevated consumer expectations around arcade quality and experience.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Posts Summer 2026 Growth but Rising Costs Squeeze Margins
articles.summary: India's amusement and entertainment sector saw attendance growth in summer 2026, but operators are facing mounting pressure from rising operational costs that are compressing profit margins. The dual dynamic of growing consumer demand alongside cost inflation is a challenge familiar to FEC operators worldwide. Suppliers and investors eyeing the Indian market should factor in the margin squeeze when modeling returns.

articles.title: India Trade Group Calls for GST Reform to Support Amusement Industry Growth
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries (IAAPI) is lobbying for GST rationalization to reduce the tax burden on amusement businesses and stimulate consumer demand. The call comes as the sector shows growth potential but struggles with cost pressures that make affordability a concern for operators and guests alike. Tax policy changes, if enacted, could significantly improve the financial outlook for FEC-style venues across India.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center Bringing Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is opening a large new facility on Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, combining an arcade with a trampoline park and other attractions. The venue is part of a broader expansion push by Launch across multiple U.S. markets, reinforcing the brand's strategy of anchoring large-format FECs in growing metro areas. Competitors and suppliers in the Southeast should monitor Launch's footprint growth closely.

articles.title: Texas's Biggest Family Entertainment Center Set to Open in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A large-scale family entertainment center billed as the biggest in Texas is slated to open in the Houston market in 2026, raising the bar for FEC scale in the state. The venue's scope signals the continued appetite among developers for mega-FEC concepts that can anchor retail and mixed-use developments. Houston-area operators should expect intensified competition for family leisure spending upon its opening.

articles.title: New Indoor Family Entertainment Center Opens in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee
articles.summary: A new indoor family entertainment center debuted in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee, over Labor Day weekend, capitalizing on one of the highest-traffic holiday periods for FEC openings. The Mt. Juliet market, part of the greater Nashville metro, continues to attract FEC investment as population growth drives demand for local entertainment options. The timing of a Labor Day opening reflects savvy market-entry strategy for new FEC operators.

articles.title: NRG Adventure Park Coming to Jacksonville's Southside
articles.summary: NRG Adventure Park has announced plans to open a new location on Jacksonville, Florida's Southside, adding another active-entertainment venue to a market seeing steady FEC growth. The park format aligns with the industry trend toward multi-attraction, physically engaging concepts that appeal to broad age ranges. Jacksonville operators should anticipate new competition for family entertainment dollars in the southern part of the metro.

articles.title: New Renderings Reveal Plans for MADCAPS Entertainment Center in Maricopa, Arizona
articles.summary: First-look renderings have been released for MADCAPS, an upcoming entertainment center in Maricopa, Arizona, giving the community and industry observers an early glimpse of the facility's design and planned attractions. The project reflects ongoing suburban FEC development driven by rapid population growth in Arizona's outer metro areas. Designers and suppliers looking for emerging market opportunities should watch the Maricopa corridor.

articles.title: The Strategic Case for In-Visit AI at Attractions
articles.summary: A new analysis from Attractions.io argues that the attractions industry is underutilizing AI by focusing on pre-visit chatbots and post-visit analytics while neglecting the high-value hours when guests are actually on-site. In-visit AI could unlock significant secondary spend in food, retail, and premium experiences at a time when attendance is flat but revenue is growing. FEC operators should evaluate how real-time, on-premises AI tools can increase per-cap spending and guest satisfaction.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso executive Lee Cowie outlines how the company is moving beyond ticketing into broader AI-driven guest experience and data analytics solutions for attractions operators. The piece highlights how data integration across the guest journey can help FEC operators make smarter operational and revenue decisions. This is essential reading for operators evaluating their technology stack and vendor partnerships.

articles.title: InPark Magazine Issue 111: Frictionless Future for Attractions Technology
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's latest issue focuses on making the guest experience as friction-free as possible across ticketing, in-park purchasing, and attraction design. Topics include AI-powered experiences, Halloween premium events, and how technology vendors like accesso and Jora Vision are reshaping guest engagement. FEC operators will find actionable insights across multiple operational areas in this edition.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Competitive Socializing Portfolio with New Game Concepts
articles.summary: Jora Vision is broadening its competitive socializing offerings with new interactive game concepts designed to drive social engagement and repeat visitation at entertainment venues. The competitive socializing trend has been one of the strongest growth areas in the FEC sector, and Jora Vision's expansion signals continued investment in the category. FEC operators looking to differentiate their offerings should review the new concepts.

articles.title: InPark Editor: Let the Guest Experience Lead Technology Decisions
articles.summary: InPark Magazine publisher Martin Palicki argues that technology investments at attractions should always serve the guest experience first, cautioning against tech-for-tech's-sake implementations. The editorial frames the broader theme of the issue: removing friction between guests and the experiences they came for. This perspective is particularly relevant for FEC operators weighing capital expenditures on new technology platforms.

articles.title: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Invest in Premium Interactive Horror with The Conjuring: Beyond Fear
articles.summary: Six Flags is partnering with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences and Plague Productions to deliver a premium interactive horror experience called The Conjuring: Beyond Fear for the Halloween season. The initiative reflects a broader industry shift toward charging premium prices for elevated, immersive Halloween events rather than relying solely on traditional haunted house formats. FEC operators running seasonal scare events should study this model for upcharge experience development.

articles.title: Efteling and TU Delft Launch SafeStrap to Enable Roller Coaster Access for Guests with Leg Prostheses
articles.summary: Efteling, in collaboration with Delft University of Technology and De Hoogstraat Rehabilitation, has introduced SafeStrap, a device that allows guests with leg prostheses to ride roller coasters without removing them. The innovation advances accessibility in the attractions industry and sets a new benchmark for inclusive ride design that other operators may be encouraged or required to adopt. FEC and amusement park operators should monitor regulatory and reputational implications of this development for their own ride accessibility policies.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Cuts Hollywood Bowl Target Price as Summer Heatwave Dents Indoor Footfall
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank has lowered its price target for Hollywood Bowl after a summer heatwave reduced indoor footfall at the bowling operator's UK venues, highlighting how extreme weather events can materially impact FEC revenue. The analyst action serves as a reminder that climate and weather volatility are financial risks for indoor entertainment operators, even those with climate-controlled venues. Operators and investors should factor weather sensitivity into business planning and financial modeling.

articles.title: Pomvom Appoints Deborah Eicher as VP Global Sales to Drive FEC and Attraction Growth
articles.summary: AI-powered digital content and guest experience company Pomvom has named Deborah Eicher as Vice President of Global Sales and Business Development, tasking her with expanding the company's commercial footprint across theme parks, attractions, and entertainment destinations. Eicher brings over two decades of industry experience to the role. The hire signals Pomvom's ambition to scale its AI-driven content solutions across the broader FEC and attractions market.

articles.title: Dream Garden Delivers Custom Multi-Level Play Environment for KIDDO FEC in Venezuela
articles.summary: Chinese manufacturer Dream Garden Amusement Equipment created a bespoke multi-level indoor play environment for KIDDO, a branded family entertainment destination at Centro San Ignacio in Caracas, Venezuela. The project combined active play, physical challenges, and themed elements within a compact commercial footprint, demonstrating the operator's focus on brand differentiation over standard playground formats. FEC developers seeking custom playground solutions for branded venues will find this a useful case study in international project delivery.

articles.title: Interstellar Arc Closes at Area15 After Less Than One Year
articles.summary: Interstellar Arc, an immersive attraction at the popular Area15 experiential complex in Las Vegas, has shuttered after operating for less than a year. The quick closure raises questions about sustainability and audience appetite for standalone immersive art experiences at premium price points. FEC and immersive entertainment operators should examine what drove the short run as a data point in evaluating similar attraction investments.

articles.title: Out-of-Home Advertising Becomes Critical as Guest Decision Windows Shrink
articles.summary: New research shows that entertainment and attractions audiences are increasingly making same-day decisions about where to spend leisure time, making out-of-home advertising a critical channel for staying visible at the moment of decision. OOH ranked as the fifth-largest source of awareness in a post-show survey, ahead of television, TikTok, and newspapers. FEC marketers should reconsider their channel mix to ensure strong OOH presence near their venues.

articles.title: Attraktion! Product Catalogue Installed at Polish Adventure Park
articles.summary: Attractions supplier Attraktion! has completed an installation of its product range at an adventure park in Poland, marking continued European expansion for the company. The project demonstrates growing demand for turnkey attraction solutions in Central and Eastern European leisure markets. FEC operators and developers in the region should evaluate Attraktion!'s portfolio for new venue builds and attraction refreshes.

articles.title: IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 Preview: Key Themes, Exhibitors, and Innovations
articles.summary: IAAPA Expo Europe returns to ExCeL London from September 21-25, 2026, with a trade show floor open September 22-24. The UK attractions market is forecast to see spending grow from £991 million to over £1.57 billion by 2027, and the expo will showcase new ride systems, immersive experiences, sustainability innovations, and guest engagement technology. FEC operators and suppliers planning to attend should use this preview to prioritize meetings and product evaluations.

articles.title: Aardman to Showcase Wallace & Gromit and Shaun the Sheep IP for FEC Licensing at IAAPA Expo Europe
articles.summary: Aardman is bringing an experiential licensing programme to IAAPA Expo Europe in London, highlighting opportunities for attractions operators to incorporate beloved characters like Wallace & Gromit and Shaun the Sheep into their venues. The studio's 50th anniversary in 2026 is expected to generate significant marketing momentum that could amplify the value of licensing deals. FEC operators seeking proven family-friendly IP for themed experiences should explore Aardman's offerings at the expo.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Creating Interactive Attraction Experiences
articles.summary: Interactive dark ride and experience designer Alterface is marking its 25th anniversary, reflecting on a legacy of creating shooting rides, interactive shows, and immersive attractions for venues worldwide. The milestone is an opportunity to examine how interactive technology has evolved and where it is headed for FEC and theme park operators. Operators considering interactive ride or experience additions should look at Alterface's expanding portfolio.

articles.title: WildBrain CPLG to Lead Location-Based Licensing for Miraculous IP Across EMEA and APAC
articles.summary: WildBrain CPLG has been appointed to manage location-based entertainment opportunities for the Miraculous brand across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific. The popular animated property, with strong appeal among children and tweens, presents a potential licensing opportunity for FEC operators seeking fresh IP for themed zones, events, or attractions. Operators in the covered regions should engage with WildBrain CPLG to explore partnership possibilities.
